### ex-the-sorgenfrey-line-is-lindelof-and-its-square-is-not — REFUSE
CURRENT TEXT READ: `title: "$\\mathbb{R}$ with the half-open intervals $[a,b)$ as a basis is not compact and, assuming the Axiom of Countable Choice, is Lindel\\\"of, while its square is not Lindel\\\"of, the antidiagonal being an uncountable closed discrete subspace"`; `[L3] The order of [[def-real-order]] makes $\mathbb{R}$ a totally ordered field ([[thm-reals-ordered-field]]) with the least-upper-bound property ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]), hence a complete ordered field ([[def-complete-ordered-field]]); for every real $t$ there is therefore $n \in \mathbb{N}$ with $t < \iota(n)$ ([[thm-of-archimedean]], [[def-canonical-natural]]); and for reals $c<d$ there is a rational strictly between them ([[lem-of-q-dense]]).`; `In the square each point $(x,-x)$ of the antidiagonal has a basic box around it meeting the antidiagonal in that point alone, and there are uncountably many such points; no countability of the rationals helps, because those boxes are pairwise distinct and each of them isolates one antidiagonal point, so an at most countable subfamily of the cover they generate can reach only at most countably many of them.`
ASSESSMENT: The repaired passages are mathematically correct. The cited targets say “Order on the reals”, “The reals form a totally ordered field”, “The Cauchy-sequence reals have the least-upper-bound property”, “Complete ordered field (least-upper-bound property)”, “Every complete ordered field is Archimedean”, “the canonical naturals are cofinal”, “canonical natural”, and “ℚ is dense in every Archimedean ordered field”. These license every part of L3. The title honestly records the Countable Choice used in step 4.1, and the corrected antidiagonal sentence follows from step 2.3. However, step 3.2 is still incorrectly cited: it declares the rational-endpoint family at most countable “by [L4] as a subfamily of a set indexed by pairs of rationals”, but no target cited in L4 states that a product of two countable sets is countable. The needed on-disk target is thm-product-of-countable, whose title says “A product of two at most countable sets is at most countable”; it is absent from both deps and L4. Likewise, L4’s assertion that an injection into an at most countable set implies countability is not the Statement of any target it cites; the corresponding on-disk target is lem-subset-of-countable, titled “Every subset of an at most countable set is at most countable”, and it too is absent. These are load-bearing citation-fidelity defects in steps 3.1 and 3.2.
COLLATERAL: none caused by the repair; both new L3 dependencies are declared, all labels remain intact, and no old proposition survives elsewhere. The refusal concerns independent surviving citation defects.
STAMPS: the verification block contains only `precheck: pass`; it has no judge, audited, or verified stamp. That is correct after the material repair.

0 certified, 1 refused.
